newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Digitel sees exponential growth in 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Digitel sees exponential growth in 5 yrs.

text.p: Digital Telecommunications Philippines Inc (Digitel) is projected to post a 54.7 percent compounded net income growth rate in the next five years, Digitel officials said on Tuesday.

"Net income is estimated to post a compounded annual growth rate of 54.7 percent from 707 million pesos in 1996 to 9.71 billion in year 2001," Eric Severino, senior vice president, said in an analysts' briefing.
The company registered a net income of 170.936 million pesos in 1995, up from 26.088 million pesos the previous year.
Severino said an aggressive and accelerated roll-out programme is expected to boost its customers' base.
The company has about 134,000 lines installed as of September this year and is scheduled to increase it to 1.2 million lines by year 2005.

It is undertaking a 10-year, 44.5 billion peso programme to expand and upgrade its existing fixed telephone network. Among the major acquisitions are submarine cable networks and personal communications network equipment.

Senior vice president Johnson Go said the commissioning of a domestic transit exchange with phone leader Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) before the end of the year will help PLDT and Digitel track better domestic calls among their users.
Digitel is the second largest fixed line provider in the country, next to PLDT.

It serves the major industrial provinces in the main island of Luzon. At present, its service area has only a 0.9 telephone density index as compared to the national average of 2.01 telephones for every 100 population.
Digitel is currently 59.3 percent owned by Philippine conglomerate JG Summit Holdings, 11.8 percent by Telia AB of Sweden, and 3.0 percent by Jasmine International Overseas Co Ltd of Thailand.
The telephone company is selling 20 percent of its total equity, or a total of 1.2 billion primary shares, to the public at 3.00 pesos per share.
